dataset: Generic red-flag phrasings that must be referenced, not repeated
purpose: Turns a HUMAN adjudication into a machine rule. When review confirms that a red-flag sentence is generic and already covered by a registered safety_flag, the phrasing is recorded here — and from then on validate-symptom-standard Y15 blocks it, so the same boilerplate cannot come back under a new record.
policy: Detection of verbatim duplication is NOT blocking (that is note N3). Blocking on exact match would reward paraphrase: an agent rewrites '突發劇烈頭痛' as '突然出現非常嚴重的頭痛', the check goes quiet, and the boilerplate survives with the signal destroyed. Worse than not checking.
Y15 blocks only on an entry in THIS file — i.e. only where a human has already decided that this wording belongs to that safety_flag. The machine never makes that call itself.
This is a boilerplate ratchet: entries only ever get added, and each one closes a phrasing permanently.
maps_to must be an id in data/config/safety_flag_vocabulary.json.
Adding an entry is a review decision, not a cleanup task. If a phrasing is genuinely specific to one symptom, it does NOT belong here even if it happens to appear twice.

field_definitions.phrasing_zh: the exact string as written on a card
field_definitions.maps_to: safety_flag id that already covers it
field_definitions.note: why this wording is generic rather than symptom-specific
